scout.d: +1 damage to friendlies in the four adjacent cells. Carries no weapon of its own.

recon.d: Spotter sweep. Calls in two more cards and is gone — no airframe to shoot down, no tile tied up. Best on turn one, when the hand is what you are short of.

pathfinder.d: Forward scout. On deployment it claims the two tiles directly ahead as your ground. Strong opening land grab, ordinary once the lines are set.

vanguard.d: Fights hardest before it is bloodied — 3 extra damage while at full hull. Deploy it early and it hits like a Specialist; let it take a scratch and it is a Rifleman.

rifle.d: 2 damage to the first hostile in the lane. The baseline body.

ab.d: Heal every adjacent personnel unit for 4 instead of the unit ahead.

medic.d: Patches every friendly in the four adjacent cells for 2 each turn. No weapon, no burst, no heroics.

archer.d: Looses into a hook: two cells straight ahead, plus the two diagonals behind it. Covers its own flanks while it shoots forward.

assassin.d: Deploys on ANY tile, including hostile ground. 4 damage to one adjacent hostile — up, down, left or right. Fragile behind the line.

samurai.d: Cuts all eight cells surrounding it for 2. The only Common that can answer something emerging behind you.

marks.d: Hits the FURTHEST hostile in the lane, ignoring everything in front. 5 on play, then 3.

lancer.d: Strikes all three cells directly ahead at once. 3 on play, then 2.

mortar.d: Indirect fire. 3x3 centred exactly four cells ahead. Cannot hit anything closer.

ab.d: Shield holds against two attacks this turn instead of one.

bulwark.d: A one-cell energy shield that IS the wall. Deploys on any held tile, occupies nothing in front. Absorbs one attack per turn and regenerates. Mobile.

ronin.d: Twin blades. Cuts the cell directly ahead AND the cell directly behind in the same motion. Nothing flanks a Ronin.

naginata.d: Polearm reach. Strikes both cells one and two ahead. Cheap pressure that outranges a blade.

kunoichi.d: Deploys on ANY tile. Strikes only the four diagonals — blind to what is directly beside her, lethal to what is not.

herald.d: Battle standard. +1 damage to every friendly in the same lane. Pairs with Scout adjacency and Relay columns.

wall.d: No weapon, no shield, no legs. Twelve hull that blocks the lane in both directions.

supply.d: Drops a munitions pallet on landing: +2 deploy points immediately, so it pays for itself and then some. Worth most on an opening turn with points to spare.

beacon.d: Plants a landing marker that claims the three cells ahead of it the moment it touches down. Strongest while the middle of the field is still neutral.

cache.d: Crack it open for 3 extra deploy points this turn — but the scramble costs you a card at random from your hand. Best on turn one when the hand is deep and the board is empty.

shield.d: Attach to a unit. Absorbs the next incoming attack entirely, then breaks.

cannon.d: Attach to a unit. It fires a second time each turn. Scales with whatever it is bolted to.

turret.d: Anchored. 2 damage to the first hostile in the lane. Eight hull, no legs.

relay.d: +1 damage to every friendly in its column, across all five lanes.

techblade.d: Sweeps a vertical arc — three cells top to bottom in the column directly ahead. Hits across lanes without leaving its own.

pulse.d: Anchored resonator. Pulses all eight surrounding cells for 1 every turn. Weak alone, brutal behind a wall.

scrambler.d: Field disruptor. Every hostile in its lane deals 1 less damage. Does not stack with itself.

battery.d: Anchored particle lance. 4 damage at exactly three cells — direct fire, so a blocker of yours cuts the beam.

knight.d: Shield and blade. Blocks the lane, regenerates its shield, and ripostes for 1 against anything that strikes it. Personnel — a Medic can patch it, a Tech Medic cannot.

ab.d: Every friendly in this lane gains a shield this turn.

aegis.d: Armoured tech frames — two cells deep, eighteen hull, regenerating energy shields and swords. Seals a lane against chip damage indefinitely.

biomed.d: Healing over time. Applies regeneration to every Common unit in its column — 2 hull per turn, refreshed while it lives.

ab.d: Burst-repair every Tech unit in the column for 8 and restore broken shields.

techmed.d: Burst repair. Trickles 2 per turn to Tech in its column, or dumps 8 at once on the ability.

ab.d: Vault and strike any hostile exactly two cells away in any direction for 6.

dragoon.d: Strikes at a fixed range of two cells ahead for 4. Thrusters let it leap and hit anything two cells out in any direction.

railgun.d: Piercing shot down the entire lane, hitting every hostile in it and ignoring armour floors. 4 on play, then 3.

hell.d: Two pods dropped behind hostile lines, on ANY tile. Each strikes all eight surrounding cells for 2. Orbital impact damages on landing.

plasma.d: Plasma barrage, 3x3 at exactly four cells. The plasma lingers two turns, burning anything standing in it and denying capture.

ab.d: Barrel two cells forward. Anything struck takes 8 and is stunned for a turn.

exo.d: Explosive hammer in an exo frame. Twenty hull, 5 damage adjacent, and a charge that shatters whatever it collides with.

zaku.d: Two bodies for one requisition. Neither will be missed and that is rather the point.

cipher.d: Trades places with any friendly unit on the board, anywhere. Uses its action for the turn.

engineer.d: No weapon. The Tech unit directly ahead hits for +2 and repairs 2 hull every turn.

outrider.d: Charges two cells. Whatever it strikes takes the hit and is driven back a cell.

fob.d: Deploys only on ground you already hold, in columns three and beyond. Adjacent friendlies repair 2 per turn and cool down a turn faster. Immobile.

mine.d: Six damage to the first hostile that enters, then spent. Visible — hostiles route around mined lanes when they can.

hecate.d: Reaches the furthest hostile on the board, any lane, for eight. Needs a turn to cycle — it cannot fire twice running.

dynamo.d: Generates +1 deploy point at the start of each turn while it stands, stacking up to +2. No weapon, thin hull — greed responsibly.

ashigaru.d: Three spear-levies drop from one requisition — thin alone, a wall in numbers.

pikewall.d: Braced spears that hold the ground they strike — reach and a body to back it, where a Naginata only has the reach.

sentry.d: No shield, no regeneration — just a blade that answers twice as hard as it is struck.

falconer.d: Armed, unlike the Recon Lark — calls in one more card and can still hold a rifle.

rampart.d: The paid middle ground between a free Barricade that cannot bite and a Bulwark that shields — nine hull, one gun, no drama.

piercer.d: Anchored railspike, fixed at exactly three cells. Armour floors mean nothing to it — a blocker of yours still cuts the beam.

suppressor.d: Field disruptor, twice over. Every hostile in its lane deals 2 less damage — a standalone answer where a Scrambler needed a second copy to match it.

reactor.d: The high-roll cousin of the Supply Drone — a bigger pallet, a thinner hull. Pays for itself and then some on an opening turn.

bore.d: Tech Blade's vertical arc, anchored and armour-piercing. Trades the legs for a beam that ignores what a floor was supposed to stop.

kessen.d: Deploys on ANY tile. Six damage to one adjacent hostile in any direction — an Assassin's kit built for a Specialist's price.

ram.d: Twice an Outrider's reach, and built to hold the ground it takes instead of riding through it.

marshal.d: Command presence. The only card that buffs its lane and its column at once — a Herald and a Relay in one requisition.

longshot.d: Hits the furthest hostile in the lane — through anything in the way. No burst, no mercy, just distance.

sapper.d: Deploys on ANY tile, including hostile ground. Strikes both cells ahead of wherever it lands — planted deep, it opens up on the hive's own rear.

rearguard.d: Faces the wrong way on purpose. Strikes the nearest hostile BEHIND it in the lane, at any range — the only ranged answer to something already past your line.

backstop.d: Calls one volley down across both home columns, every lane at once, for 5. Anything standing there breaches on the next step — this is the last word before it does. Fired once, then spent.

servo.d: May move AND fire in the same turn.

coolant.d: Ability cooldowns are 1 turn shorter, minimum 1.

phase.d: The first killing blow leaves it at 1 hull instead. Once per deployment.

weave.d: +1 shield capacity. Stacks with regenerating shields.

dropod.d: May deploy straight onto a hostile below Specialist tier, crushing it on landing and holding the cell.

stim.d: +2 damage. The unit loses 1 hull every turn it lives.

ifield.d: Immune to indirect fire — Mortar, Plasma Artillerist, anything that arcs.

twinlink.d: May move AND fire in the same turn. +1 damage.

adaptive.d: +4 hull. +1 shield capacity, stacks with regenerating shields.

overclock.d: Ignores hostile armour floors. Ability cooldowns are 1 turn shorter, minimum 1.

ghostplate.d: The first killing blow leaves it at 1 hull instead, once per deployment. +1 shield capacity.

rapidkit.d: Costs 1 less deploy point, minimum 1. May move AND fire in the same turn.

opticsrelay.d: Direct fire ignores blockers in the lane — reaches whatever the weapon would otherwise be denied.

rearsights.d: Also strikes the cell directly behind this unit. Nothing flanks it.

crawler.d: Cheap, fast, endless. Moves two cells a turn and floods whatever lane you leave open.

breacher.d: Prioritises Tech over personnel. Punishes Barricade and Turret spam.

spitter.d: Stops at range four and fires down the lane. Outranges most of your roster. Punishes turtling.

burrower.d: Emerges mid-board, behind your front line. Punishes over-committing forward.

hulk.d: Slow, heavy, reduces all incoming damage by 1. Punishes chip damage.

spore.d: Immobile emplacement. Releases a Crawler every two turns and holds its tile until destroyed.

pylon.d: Immobile emplacement. +1 damage floor to every hostile in its lane.

jammer.d: Immobile emplacement. Blocks all indirect fire in its lane. Shuts off Mortar and Artillerist entirely.

harrower.d: Tunnels straight past blockers. Barricades and Bulwarks do not stop it.

chorus.d: Immobile at the far edge. +1 damage to every hostile on the board. Kill it first — if you can reach it.

sovereign.d: Moves every other turn. Every tile it crosses becomes hostile ground permanently.

husk.d: Shambles forward and falls apart when destroyed — two Crawlers crawl out of the wreck. Kill it somewhere you can afford the mess.

mender.d: Carries no weapon. Advances with the horde and knits 2 hull back into the most wounded hostile in its lane every turn. Kill it first.

screamer.d: Dies loudly. The scream sends every hostile on the board one step forward — time the kill, or the kill times you.

puppeteer.d: Never moves. Every 3 turns it seizes the nearest unit in its lane, turning it against you until it breaks free or the Puppeteer dies.

ironbrand.bio: Held the Sundering Gate for nine days with a company of forty. Believes armour is a philosophy.

passive.d: Every unit you deploy arrives with +1 hull.

wildfire.bio: Three commendations, two demotions, one very expensive orbital incident. Fights fast and asks after.

coldwire.bio: Speaks to machines more than people. The machines, notably, keep working.

passive.d: All your units repair 1 hull at the end of every turn.

loneedge.bio: Treats every engagement as a private duel. Plunges into the centre of a formation and trusts the squad to keep up or stay clear.

passive.d: A unit with no friendly in an adjacent cell deals +2 damage.

skunkworks.bio: Ex-skunkworks, permanently caffeinated, trusts machines over orders. Treats the battlefield as a laboratory with inconvenient variables.

passive.d: Tech units deploy with +2 hull and repair 1 hull every turn.

quietstep.bio: Soft-spoken until the unit initialises. Moves through a turn like a rumour and neutralises threats before they resolve.

passive.d: Cards that deploy on hostile ground cost 1 less deploy point, minimum 1.

firebrand.bio: Walked away from a military pedigree to fight at the line. Argues with command, never with her squad.

passive.d: +2 deploy points on any turn after you lost a unit.

riptide.bio: Treats a firefight like a contact sport. No patience for planning, uncanny instinct for where the line is about to break.

passive.d: Units that repositioned this turn take 1 less damage.

stronghold.d: Hold the line through every wave. Each lane's grid charge absorbs one breach — after that, one body through ends it.

civilians.d: A shelter holds the line while survivors run for the edge. Protect it, walk enough of them out, and the block is clear.

specimens.d: Destroy the marked hostile type to fill the quota.

crystals.d: Four crystal nodes on the field. Hold three when the last wave clears.

retake.d: Hold 3 or more tiles in the hostile half when the last wave clears. Bring something that deploys behind their line.

extract.d: Short and heavy. Survive to extraction.

uplink.d: A relay tile sits in contested ground. Hold it three turns in a row to bring the uplink online.

blitz.d: Purge the zone. Destroy ten hostiles before the wave count runs out.

blackout.d: No wave preview and no spawn markers.

crumble.d: Every couple of turns, one open tile collapses for good — impassable to both sides.

ironveil.sub: Delta Shelf · orbital shipyard, no transmission
ironveil.lore:
The Delta Shelf yards built half the fleet holding this sector. Three weeks ago a cluster of small meteors struck the facility. Two weeks later, all transmission went silent.

Command doesn't believe in coincidences.

Secure the facility and salvage the hulls in dock before the structure gives. The yards are worth far more than the rock they sit on — failure to retrieve them is not an option.

nodes.reqText: Power offline — reset the Power Junction in the Deep Shaft

blackmarrow.lore: The Blackmarrow seams run deeper than any survey admits, and something has been hollowing them out from below. The last crew up sealed the winch station behind them and never said what they saw. The nest is confirmed. Burn it out — and mind the dark below the second gallery, where the power has been out for a month.

sunderglass.lore: The Sunderglass flats grow the resonant crystal every jump drive in the sector depends on, and the hive grazes on them like cattle. Every day the fields sit contested, the harvest shatters a little more. Cut what can still be saved and get out before the glassing swallows the route home.

nodes.lore: The research data lives here. Hold the uplink while it pulls.

nodes.reqText: The research data is still in the spire — secure the Archive Core first

nodes.lore: Survivors barricaded in the dorms. Walking them out is optional — and paid.

lumenspire.lore: Meridian City evacuated in six hours; the Lumenspire research division never made the manifest. Whatever their labs were close to, command wants it badly enough to send a squad back into a dead city for it. The researchers barricaded in the dorms are listed as an optional objective. Their families have been told otherwise.

crownring.sub: Concordat summit · burrowers inside the walls

nodes.lore: The faction reps move on foot. Walk them through the ward.

nodes.reqText: The delegations leave first — clear the Northgate route

crownring.lore: Once a year the Concordat factions meet under one roof to keep the alliance stitched together. This year the burrowers came up through the foundations mid-session — past every checkpoint, straight for the Summit Hall. If the delegations die in the wards, the alliance dies with them and the whole region tips. Walk them out. Whatever it costs.

shallowhelm.sub: Fortress Shallow Helm · gone dark, no distress call

nodes.lore: Restore the couplings. Hold them while they spin up.
The garrison’s last logs. Optional — command pays well for answers.

nodes.reqText: No power on the deck — restore the Power Vault first

nodes.lore: Arm the Self-Cleanse and purge everything it flushes at you.

nodes.reqText: The Self-Cleanse is not armed — fight back to the Cleanse Core first

shallowhelm.lore: Fortress Shallow Helm held the pass for forty years and never missed a check-in. Nine days ago it simply stopped — no distress call, no survivors on the walls, the gates sealed from the inside. Whatever is in there now wears the Helm like a shell. Put the fortress through its own Self-Cleanse, and come back out the way you went in.

targeting.archer: Two ahead plus both rear diagonals
targeting.vert3: Three cells vertically, one column ahead
targeting.bothsides: The cell ahead and the cell behind
targeting.ahead2: Both cells one and two ahead
targeting.rear: Nearest hostile BEHIND it in the lane

duel.d: One unit gains +4 damage and takes no damage until your next turn.

refit.d: Every Tech unit you control is restored to full hull.

insertion.d: The next three units you deploy this turn may land on any tile, held or not.

breach.d: Destroy every hostile in the chosen column that is at or below 8 hull.

grapple.d: Drag every hostile in the chosen lane two cells back toward their edge.

requisition.d: +4 deploy points when the call lands.
